iHeartMedia fell ~29% premarket after its Q3 2026 report; no further detail (reported figures, consensus comparison) located beyond the aggregator mover headline this session.
iHeartMedia CEO warned major advertisers are delaying spending as economic uncertainty bites, cited as driver of continued share weakness the day after earnings

iHeartMedia Q3 2026 results: revenue $1.03B (+3.3% YoY, +1% ex-political); Adjusted EBITDA $170.5M, down 16.7% YoY and below the company's own $180-220M plan; GAAP EPS loss of $0.06 (vs -$0.02 est.); Multiplatform Group (broadcast) segment adjusted EBITDA fell 42.9%; Digital Audio Group revenue +13.8% but segment EBITDA -2.3%; podcast revenue +24.4% to $173.7M; free cash flow -$10.4M for the quarter; cash fell to $139.7M from $174.4M at June 2026; company cut full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $550M-$600M from the prior ~$800M target cited on prior calls, largely on weaker-than-expected political advertising, advertiser spending delays amid macro uncertainty, and a shift to programmatic audio buying
catalysts.impact: Shares fell sharply; reported after-hours decline of approximately 35-37%, with the stock later touching a new 52-week low intraday around -66% to $0.598-$0.6095 before settling near $0.62
